header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #177 (reconciliation gate hardening). Read the issue first (`gh issue view 177`).

Goal: a bank statement draft is "reconciled" only when every row is accounted for and correctly signed, and nothing the model returns is silently dropped or stored unvalidated. Project rule: parsers fail loudly (Left), never invent defaults.

Scope (server only): `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/AiStatementExtractor.scala`, `.../actions/bankstatements/UpdateBankStatementDraftAction.scala`, `.../actions/bankstatements/ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.scala`, `BankStatementDraftLimits`, and `BankStatementDraftReconciliation.scala` if needed.

Work:
1. `verify` (AiStatementExtractor, chain branch around lines 163-212): when a closing balance exists, require the last running balance to equal it within the existing tolerance (either sign convention as today). An empty row list is never reconciled. Confirm must reject an empty draft.
2. `parseAndVerify` (around lines 88-101): a transaction element that fails to parse must produce a Left that feeds the existing retry-with-feedback loop, instead of being dropped. Only return rows when all parsed.
3. One payload validator (field lengths, bounded two-decimal amounts, enum values for txnType and productType, ISO currency code) called after parsing, on draft update, and at confirm. Remove the `"purchase"` default for a missing type in ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction (around line 106): missing type must fail.
4. Use `productType` to pick the expected sign convention. Decision already made: credit-card statements stay sign-agnostic as today (intentional, tested). For debit/checking accounts require the running-balance chain and the opening/closing net check to hold under the debit convention (balance_i = balance_{i-1} + amount_i, charges negative); the opposite convention is a blocking validation failure, not a pass.

Out of scope (separate follow-up, do not do here): making extracted anchors immutable server-side against client edits.

Acceptance (add regression tests that fail before and pass after; follow docs/guide/testing.md):
- AiStatementExtractorSpec: chain holds but last balance differs from closing (e.g. opening 100.00, closing 10.00, one row -40.00 with balance 60.00 must NOT reconcile); zero rows with an opening balance must NOT reconcile; one malformed row among valid ones returns Left; fully sign-inverted debit statement is rejected; three-decimal amount rejected.
- Draft controller/action spec: confirm of an empty draft rejected; out-of-range or malformed edit rejected on update.
- Existing credit-statement tests still pass. Use placeholder data only (the repo is public), no real merchants or amounts, no external calls in tests.
- Per the repo rules: run targeted specs, scalafmtAll + scalafmtSbt, and follow CLAUDE.md. Commit messages must not contain Claude session links.

resultJson.description:
Harden the bank-statement reconciliation gate (GitHub issue #177) so that a draft counts as "reconciled" only when every row is accounted for and has the right sign. Also make sure nothing the AI model returns is silently dropped or stored without validation. Today `AiStatementExtractor.verify` has three gaps. (a) It never compares the last running balance with the closing balance, so a truncated extraction whose rows still chain from the opening balance counts as reconciled. (b) It reconciles an empty row list, because `forall`/`sum` over Nil is trivially true. (c) It accepts either sign convention whatever the `productType`, so a debit statement with every sign flipped passes. In addition, `parseAndVerify` silently `flatMap`s away transaction elements that fail to parse, and the confirm step stores a fabricated `"purchase"` type when a row has none.

The fix stays in the server and follows the project rule that parsers fail loudly (`Left` or an exception) and never invent defaults. Reconciliation rules: a closing balance, when present, must match the end of the chain (same 0.01 tolerance, either sign). An empty draft is never reconciled and is rejected at confirm. Debit statements must satisfy the debit convention (balance_i = balance_{i-1} + amount_i, charges negative). The opposite convention becomes a blocking discrepancy. Credit statements stay sign-agnostic on purpose. A malformed transaction element becomes a `Left`, which feeds the existing retry-with-feedback loop in `StatementExtractionService`. One pure payload validator covers field lengths, amounts bounded to 10 integer and 2 fraction digits, enum values for `txnType` and `productType`, and ISO-4217 currency. It runs after parsing, on draft update (only for edited values, keeping the existing rule that unchanged stored values are exempt) and in full at confirm.

Out of scope: making extracted anchors (opening, closing, per-row balances, row count) immutable server-side against client edits. That is a separate follow-up. No web/frontend changes, no DB evolutions, no Tapir endpoint changes.

tasks.title: Require closing-balance match and reject empty rows in reconciliation; reject empty drafts at confirm
tasks.description:
In `AiStatementExtractor.verify` (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/AiStatementExtractor.scala:160-212):
1. If `txns.isEmpty`, return `Verification(reconciled = false, unverifiable = false, Some(<message saying there are no transactions>), None)` before any chain or net check. This covers both paths: today the chain fold over Nil returns `Some(true)`, and the net check passes when opening == closing.
2. In the chain branch, once the chain holds, if `meta.closingBalance` is `Some(c)`, also require `last = txns.last.runningBalance.get` to satisfy `min(|last - c|, |last + c|) < Tolerance` (either sign convention, as today). Otherwise return reconciled=false, unverifiable=false, a discrepancy such as "The running balance ends at $last but the closing balance is $c; rows are likely missing.", and `residual = Some(gap)` so that `bestOf` can rank the result. If the closing balance is absent, the chain alone decides, as today.

In `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.apply`, reject a payload with `transactions.isEmpty` explicitly, before `requireReconciled`, with a `RuntimeException`. Keep the word "reconcile" in the message (e.g. "The draft has no transactions, so it can't be reconciled or imported"), because the existing controller test at BankStatementDraftControllerSpec.scala:811 asserts `include("reconcile")`.

Tests (each must fail before the change):
- AiStatementExtractorSpec, parseAndVerify: opening 100.00, closing 10.00, one row -40.00 with runningBalance 60.00 must NOT reconcile (unverifiable false, discrepancy defined).
- AiStatementExtractorSpec, reconcile: `reconcile(Some(100.00), Some(10.00), List((-40.00, Some(60.00))))` is not reconciled. `reconcile(Some(100.00), None, Nil)` and `reconcile(Some(100.00), Some(100.00), Nil)` are both not reconciled and not unverifiable.
- A new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ConfirmBankStatementDraftActionSpec.scala` (a `RepositorySpec` with `RepositoryUtils`; see how CreateBankStatementDraftFromCsvActionSpec builds `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`): confirming a ready draft with full valid metadata, opening 100.00 = closing 100.00 and `transactions = Nil` fails and leaves the draft in place.

All existing AiStatementExtractorSpec, UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec and StatementExtractionServiceSpec cases must still pass. Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *AiStatementExtractorSpec *ConfirmBankStatementDraftActionSpec *UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec *StatementExtractionServiceSpec"`.

tasks.title: Pick the sign convention from productType: debit statements must use the debit convention
tasks.description:
Make `verify` take the product type into account.
- For `meta.productType == Some(ProductType.Debit)`: the chain may only use `sign = 1`, and the opening/closing net check may only use `sumAll - (c - o)`.
- For Credit or None: keep today's behaviour, accepting either sign (`sign = 1 or -1`; `c - o` or `o - c`). This is intentional and tested.
- For Debit, when the debit convention fails but the opposite convention would hold (in the chain or in the net check), return reconciled=false, unverifiable=false and a specific blocking discrepancy, e.g. "The amounts have the opposite sign for a debit account: charges must be negative and deposits positive." Any other failure keeps the existing messages. The closing-balance comparison from the previous task stays sign-agnostic.

Change the public signature to `reconcile(productType: Option[ProductType], openingBalance: Option[BigDecimal], closingBalance: Option[BigDecimal], rows: List[(BigDecimal, Option[BigDecimal])]): Reconciliation` and pass it into `Meta`. Update both callers, which hold the draft's `metadata.productType: Option[String]`:
- `BankStatementDraftReconciliation.recompute` (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/BankStatementDraftReconciliation.scala)
- `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.requireReconciled`

Map the string with `ProductType.values.find(_.entryName == s.trim)`. An unknown string maps to None; the validator task makes unknown values a hard error. Update the existing `reconcile(...)` calls in AiStatementExtractorSpec to pass `None`.

Tests (fail before, pass after):
- AiStatementExtractorSpec: a fully sign-inverted debit statement with a running-balance chain (productType debit, opening 100.00, closing 60.00, row amount +40.00, runningBalance 60.00) is NOT reconciled and the discrepancy mentions the sign.
- A sign-inverted debit statement without running balances (opening 100.00, closing 60.00, row +40.00) is NOT reconciled.
- The same inverted data with productType credit still reconciles, and the existing credit test (1484.73 → 1689.69, -204.96) still passes.
- reconcile with `Some(ProductType.Debit)` and inverted rows is not reconciled.
- UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec: saving a debit draft whose rows are sign-inverted stores `reconciled = false` with a discrepancy.

Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *AiStatementExtractorSpec *UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec *StatementExtractionServiceSpec *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Fail loudly on a malformed transaction element in parseAndVerify
tasks.description:
In `AiStatementExtractor.parseAndVerify` (lines 84-132), replace the `flatMap` that silently drops elements. Parse each element of `transactions` to `Either[String, Txn]` with its 1-based index:
- `date` must be a `LocalDate`, `amount` a `BigDecimal` and `description` a `String`. If any is missing or invalid, return `Left(s"Transaction $n is malformed: missing or invalid <field>")`.
- The optional fields `runningBalance` and `type` use `(t \ "x").validateOpt[...]`, which gives `JsSuccess(None)` when the field is absent or null and `JsError` when present but of the wrong type. A present-but-invalid value is also a `Left`.

Collect the results with a short-circuit (first `Left` wins, e.g. `foldRight` or `traverse`-style), so rows are returned only when all of them parsed. Keep the existing `Left("The model extracted no transactions")` for an empty list. Don't change `StatementExtractionService`: its `Left(error)` branch already retries with the error as feedback, up to `MaxAttempts`.

Tests in AiStatementExtractorSpec (fail before, pass after):
- One malformed row (e.g. missing amount) among two valid ones returns `Left`, and the message names the row number.
- A row whose `runningBalance` is a non-numeric string returns `Left`.
- A valid statement still parses all rows.

Optionally, add a StatementExtractionServiceSpec case where the first response has a malformed row and the retry, given that error as feedback, returns a reconciling statement. Use the existing `RecordingBedrock` pattern and no external calls.

Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *AiStatementExtractorSpec *StatementExtractionServiceSpec"`.

tasks.title: Add the bank statement payload validator and apply it after parsing
tasks.description:
Create a pure validator at `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/BankStatementPayloadValidator.scala`. It must not depend on tapir or the `BankStatementDraft` models, so that AiStatementExtractor stays runnable in an isolated JVM. Suggested API:
```scala
final case class Header(bankName: Option[String], productType: Option[String], currency: Option[String], accountLast4: Option[String], openingBalance: Option[BigDecimal], closingBalance: Option[BigDecimal])
final case class Row(description: String, amount: BigDecimal, txnType: Option[String], runningBalance: Option[BigDecimal])
def validateHeader(h: Header): Either[String, Unit]
def validateRow(rowNumber: Int, r: Row): Either[String, Unit]   // 1-based
def validate(h: Header, rows: List[Row]): Either[String, Unit]  // first error wins
```
Rules. `None` is always valid here; the presence of required fields is enforced at confirm.
- Lengths come from `BankStatementDraftLimits` and are checked before the enum and format checks. Reuse the exact existing messages: "Row N: description is longer than 255 characters", "Row N: type is longer than 20 characters", "Bank name is longer than 100 characters", "Product type is longer than 20 characters", "Currency is longer than 3 characters", "Account last 4 is longer than 4 characters". Build them from the constants as UpdateBankStatementDraftAction does today.
- `txnType` must be one of the new shared `BankStatementDraftLimits.TxnTypes: List[String] = List("purchase", "payment", "fee", "interest", "refund")`. This is the set the RealBedrockClient prompt and the web `BankStatementTemplatePage.txnTypes` use. Leave the web file untouched.
- `productType` must be one of `ProductType.values.map(_.entryName)` ("credit", "debit").
- `currency` must be exactly 3 uppercase letters and present in `java.util.Currency.getAvailableCurrencies`.
- `amount`, `runningBalance`, `openingBalance` and `closingBalance` must have at most `MaxAmountFractionDigits` (2) decimal places, checked with `bigDecimal.stripTrailingZeros.scale <= 2` so that 40.00 and 40 pass, and at most `MaxAmountIntegerDigits` (10) integer digits, e.g. `abs < 1e10`. Messages say which row or field and why, e.g. "Row 2: amount 12.345 has more than 2 decimal places".

Wire it into `parseAndVerify`:
- Read `metadata.productType` as a raw `Option[String]` instead of `asOpt[ProductType]`, which silently turns an unknown value into None.
- Build Header and Rows and call `validate`. On `Left`, return that `Left`, which feeds the retry loop.
- Only then map productType to `ProductType` for `Meta`.
- `Meta`, `Txn` and the result types stay unchanged.

Tests:
- A new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/BankStatementPayloadValidatorSpec.scala` (AnyWordSpec, `must` matchers, `should` subjects naming methods, not the object). Cover: accepts valid values and None; rejects a 3-decimal amount, an 11-integer-digit amount, an unknown txnType, an unknown productType, a lowercase or unknown currency (e.g. "eur", "ZZZ"), and a 3-decimal opening balance; keeps the length messages above.
- AiStatementExtractorSpec: a statement with a three-decimal amount (e.g. -12.345) returns `Left`; an unknown productType returns `Left`.

All existing extractor and service specs must still pass; their fixtures use debit/credit, EUR and no `type`. Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *BankStatementPayloadValidatorSpec *AiStatementExtractorSpec *StatementExtractionServiceSpec"`.

tasks.title: Validate payloads on draft update and at confirm; remove the "purchase" default
tasks.description:
UpdateBankStatementDraftAction (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/UpdateBankStatementDraftAction.scala):
- Replace the private `validateEditedRows` and `validateEditedMetadata` with calls to `BankStatementPayloadValidator`, keeping the existing exemption rule that values kept exactly as stored are exempt:
  - Rows: call `validateRow(index + 1, ...)` only for rows not in `existingTxns.toSet`.
  - Metadata: build a `Header` where each field is set to None when it equals the stored value (e.g. `metadata.bankName.filter(_ => metadata.bankName != stored.bankName)`), including the opening and closing balances, then call `validateHeader`.
  - Turn a `Left(msg)` into `throw new RuntimeException(msg)`, matching the current error style. Do this before `recompute` and `updatePayload`, so a rejected edit leaves the stored payload unchanged.
- Keep the MaxTransactions growth-only rule as is. It is not part of the validator, because extracted drafts may legitimately exceed 250 rows.
- A missing txnType stays allowed on update: CSV drafts start without types and the user fills them in during review.

ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction:
- After decoding the payload, run the full `validate` with no exemption, and throw on `Left`.
- Require every row to have a txnType, e.g. "Row N: type is missing".
- Replace `t.txnType.getOrElse("purchase")` (line 106) with the validated value. No default.
- Keep the empty-draft rejection and `requireReconciled` from the earlier tasks.

Fix the test fixture that relied on the default: in CreateBankStatementDraftFromCsvActionSpec, the `confirm` helper (lines 86-104) must also set a type on rows that lack one when it calls Update (e.g. `transactions.map(t => t.copy(txnType = t.txnType.orElse(Some("purchase"))))`), and the assertion at line 273 must compare against that.

Tests (fail before, pass after):
- UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec: an edited row with a 3-decimal amount is rejected and the stored payload is unchanged; an edited row with an 11-integer-digit amount is rejected; an edited row with an unknown txnType (e.g. "bogus") is rejected; an edited currency "ZZZ" or productType "savings" is rejected. The existing length-message tests and the unchanged-value exemption tests (description and productType over the limit) still pass.
- ConfirmBankStatementDraftActionSpec: a reconciling draft with a row whose `txnType = None` is rejected and the draft stays; a draft with an invalid currency or a 3-decimal amount seeded directly into the DB is rejected at confirm; the happy path still creates the statement.

Use placeholder names ("Test Bank", "TEST MERCHANT") and round amounts. Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec *ConfirmBankStatementDraftActionSpec *CreateBankStatementDraftFromCsvActionSpec *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec"`, then run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared: shared models and limits. `net.wiringbits.api.utils.BankStatementDraftLimits` (lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/BankStatementDraftLimits.scala) holds MaxTransactions=250, MaxDescriptionLength=255, MaxTxnTypeLength=20, MaxBankNameLength=100, MaxProductTypeLength=20, MaxCurrencyLength=3, MaxAccountLast4Length=4, MaxAmountIntegerDigits=10, MaxAmountFractionDigits=2, DecimalPattern and BoundedDecimalPattern (regexes for strings, used by the CSV parser and the web forms). It is a plain object that is safe to use anywhere.
- `net.wiringbits.api.models.bankstatementtemplates.ProductType`: sealed, with `Credit("credit")` and `Debit("debit")`, `values`, `fromEntryName` (throws), and a play-json Format.
- `net.wiringbits.api.models.bankstatements.BankStatementDraft` (lib/api/shared/.../bankstatements/BankStatementDraft.scala):
  - `Metadata(bankName, productType: Option[String], currency, accountLast4: Option[String], periodStart, periodEnd: Option[LocalDate], openingBalance, closingBalance: Option[BigDecimal])`
  - `Transaction(date: LocalDate, amount: BigDecimal, description: String, txnType: Option[String], runningBalance: Option[BigDecimal])`
  - `Payload(metadata, transactions, reconciled, discrepancy, model, stage, unverifiable)`
  - The companions derive tapir Schemas. Do NOT reference these types from AiStatementExtractor or the new validator: per its scaladoc, the schema only initialises safely inside the booted app, and the extractor must run in an isolated JVM.

SERVER FILES
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/AiStatementExtractor.scala: pure parsing and verification.
  - Types: `Txn(date, amount, description, runningBalance: Option[BigDecimal], txnType: Option[String])`, `Meta(bankName, productType: Option[ProductType], currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, openingBalance, closingBalance)`, `ExtractionResult(reconciled, discrepancy, model, transactions, metadata, residual: Option[BigDecimal], source = None, unverifiable)`, `Reconciliation(reconciled, unverifiable, discrepancy)`, private `Verification(reconciled, unverifiable, discrepancy, residual)`.
  - `parseAndVerify(rawJson, model): Either[String, ExtractionResult]` (lines 84-132). Today its transactions `flatMap` drops bad elements, and it reads productType with `asOpt[ProductType]`, which silently turns unknown values into None.
  - `reconcile(opening, closing, rows: List[(BigDecimal, Option[BigDecimal])])` builds a Meta with productType None and calls `verify`.
  - `verify` (lines 160-202): the chain applies when an opening balance is present and every row has a runningBalance, and accepts sign ±1. Otherwise it runs the net check when both balances are present, with `minBy` of `sum-(c-o)` and `sum-(o-c)`. Otherwise the result is unverifiable.
  - `chainHolds(opening, txns, sign)` (lines 204-212); `Tolerance = 0.01`; `bestOf` prefers reconciled results, then non-unverifiable ones, then the minimal residual; `isTerminalUnverifiable(unverifiable, count) = unverifiable && count > 0`.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementExtractionService.scala:218-261: `extractReconciling` is the retry loop. On a `Left(error)` it retries with the error as Bedrock feedback (cached by model, feedback and text) until MaxAttempts, or stops early when the same error repeats; then it keeps the prior best or fails. A non-terminal `Right` retries with `discrepancy` as feedback. No change is needed there.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/BankStatementDraftReconciliation.scala: `recompute(payload)` calls `AiStatementExtractor.reconcile` and sets reconciled, discrepancy and unverifiable (via isTerminalUnverifiable). It is used by UpdateBankStatementDraftAction and CreateBankStatementDraftFromCsvAction.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/UpdateBankStatementDraftAction.scala:
  - Loads the draft (must be status "ready"), parses the stored payload, rejects only growth past MaxTransactions, runs `validateEditedRows` and `validateEditedMetadata`, then `recompute(request.payload.copy(model = stored.model))` and `updatePayload`.
  - Rows and metadata values kept exactly as stored are exempt from limits; this is intentional and covered by tests. Errors are `throw new RuntimeException(msg)` inside the for-comprehension, which fails the Future.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.scala: `apply(draftId, userId, acceptWarnings, acceptUnverified)` does the following:
  - Loads the draft and its document, parses the payload, and calls `requireReconciled` (lines 139-150), which reconciles again from the payload and allows unverifiable drafts only with `acceptUnverified` and at least one row.
  - Calls `requireMetadata`, which throws "Missing required metadata: ...", then builds warnings and calls `create`. `create` builds the `BankStatementRow.Create` list with `txnType = t.txnType.getOrElse("purchase")` at line 106; that default must go.
- Other `parseAndVerify` callers, whose signature is unchanged: AiExtractBankStatementAction (bankstatementtemplates) and scripts/AiExtractionProof.scala.
- `txn_type` is `TEXT NOT NULL` in the DB (evolution 3.sql), so a missing type must be rejected before insert.
- The txnType vocabulary used by the AI prompt (apis/RealBedrockClient.scala:122) and the web (BankStatementTemplatePage.txnTypes) is purchase, payment, fee, interest, refund.
- StatementCsvParser (server/.../services/StatementCsvParser.scala) produces CSV drafts whose txn_type column is optional, so a CSV draft can hold `txnType = None`. That stays allowed on update; confirm will now reject it, and the user sets the type in review.

TESTS
- Conventions (docs/guide/testing.md):
  - AnyWordSpec with `must` matchers.
  - `should` subjects are method names or scenarios and never repeat the class or object name.
  - Test files mirror source paths.
  - DB tests extend `RepositorySpec` with `RepositoryUtils`, use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }` and `.futureValue`, and use random unique data.
  - New behaviour is owned by action integration tests; BankStatementDraftControllerSpec is grandfathered, so add new cases to action specs rather than the controller spec.
  - The repo is public: use placeholder data only ("Test Bank", "TEST MERCHANT", "0000", EUR/USD, round amounts) and no external calls.
- server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/AiStatementExtractorSpec.scala: pure, with an `ok(json)` helper. Current fixtures:
  - debit 100.00 → 60.00 with a -40.00 row and balance 60.00;
  - credit 1484.73 → 1689.69 with -204.96 (uses the o-c convention and must keep passing);
  - transactions without a "type" field (so don't make type required at parse);
  - direct `reconcile(opening, closing, rows)` calls, which must be updated if the signature gains `productType`.
- server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/UpdateBankStatementDraftActionSpec.scala: has `readyDraft(initial)`, `action`, `storedPayload` and `payload(...)` helpers. It asserts exact messages such as "Row 2: description is longer than 255 characters", "Row 1: type is longer than 20 characters", "Bank name is longer than 100 characters" and "Currency is longer than 3 characters" (for "ABCD"), so length checks must come before enum and ISO checks. Its exemption tests must keep passing.
- server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/CreateBankStatementDraftFromCsvActionSpec.scala: shows how to construct `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction(repositories.bankStatementDrafts, repositories.bankStatements, repositories.documents)(using executionContext, summon[Clock])` and `UpdateBankStatementDraftAction`. Its `confirm` helper and line 273 rely on the "purchase" default for a CSV row with `txnType = None`, so they need fixing when the default is removed.
- There is no ConfirmBankStatementDraftActionSpec yet; create it at server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ConfirmBankStatementDraftActionSpec.scala. `RepositoryUtils.createBankStatementDraft(userId, sha256, filename)` plus `repositories.bankStatementDrafts.markReady(id, json, Instant.now())` seed a ready draft.
- server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementDraftControllerSpec.scala: `reconcilingPayload` (debit, 100 → 60, one -40.00 row with balance 60.00, txnType purchase, EUR) and `unverifiablePayload`. Line 811 expects an empty unverifiable draft's confirm error to `include("reconcile")`, so keep that word in the empty-draft message. `cardPayload(productType = "credit")` reuses debit-convention data and still passes because credit stays sign-agnostic.
- server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementExtractionServiceSpec.scala: JSON fixtures are all debit, EUR and debit-convention, with no "type". `chainBreak` has no closing balance. It runs the ladder with fake Bedrock, BDA and Textract recorders and must keep passing.

BUILD AND CONVENTIONS
- Targeted tests only: `sbt "server/testOnly *SpecName"` (DB specs need Docker), or `CI=true sbt Test/compile` to typecheck. Do not run the full `sbt test`.
- Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.
- Error style: pure functions return `Either[String, _]`; actions throw `RuntimeException(msg)` inside the Future for-comprehension.
- No silent defaults: never fabricate a type, currency or similar.
- Commit messages must not contain Claude session links.
- `BigDecimal` from JSON keeps its scale (12.345 has scale 3; 40.00 has scale 2). Use `bigDecimal.stripTrailingZeros.scale <= 2` for the 2-decimal rule.
- play-json `(js \ "f").validateOpt[A]` gives JsSuccess(None) when the field is missing or null and JsError when it is present but has the wrong type.
- Known flakiness (memory): BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec can race; rerun it before debugging.

findings.title: Debit closing-balance check still accepts the negated closing balance

reason.text: The task spec says explicitly: 'The closing-balance comparison from the previous task stays sign-agnostic.' Making it sign-aware for debit changes behaviour the user has fixed, so it needs their sign-off first.

findings.title: Debit chain check still accepts a negated closing balance

reason.text: Same issue as I3.2. The task spec says explicitly that the closing-balance comparison stays sign-agnostic, so changing it needs the user's approval.

findings.title: Length checks and messages are duplicated in UpdateBankStatementDraftAction

reason.text: Out of scope for this stage, which only wires the validator into parseAndVerify. Moving the update action onto the validator has to keep the unchanged-value exemption, so it belongs in the plan's separate update/confirm wiring work.

findings.title: Amount bound rules re-encoded instead of reusing the existing decimal pattern

reason.text: Kept the BigDecimal form on purpose. The validator receives parsed BigDecimals, not strings, so the regex can't be applied without converting back to a string. Sharing a helper with StatementCsvParser would touch the CSV parser, which is outside this task. The finding marks it as low priority.
